answers.question: Is the described architecture actually pinned by anything?
answers.answer: Yes, as implementation parity: compatibility key, XOR-center formula, absolute byte counter, reciprocal decrypt, and two bus paths each carrying 2,304 table bytes and a 1,024-byte payload. It is explicitly not a security proof.

reproduce.behavior: Renders deterministic playback of a preserved receipt. It runs no benchmark, no test suite, no synthesis, and no cracking run.
reproduce.workspacePathConstraint: The tape records to an absolute path under /Volumes/Code/MuleinLabs and must be adjusted if the workspace is relocated.

capturedAtBasis: Rendered during this documentation pass; the underlying experiment predates it and is dated in the receipt itself

captureMethod.mode: normal-speed playback of a preserved receipt

artifacts.kind: durable byte-for-byte copy used by the tape

timingContext.interpretation: The capture replays preserved text at normal speed. Any elapsed-time figures visible on screen are historical observations from the original run on one Apple-silicon host, not fresh measurements and not portable performance contracts.

claimBoundaries: This is playback of a preserved validation receipt, not a live run.
It is bounded implementation and parity evidence, not an IND-CPA or HMAC security proof.
Human review is pending and audit finding E256-003 remains OPEN.
AI semantic review is not human acceptance and does not close E256-003.
The receipt validates the counter in RTL; it does not implement HMAC in RTL.
Rotor-pool sizing, state-seed width, and serial-access counts are design-document claims and are not proved by this receipt.
TensorLUT artifacts here are narrow synthesized cones, not the full E256 core.
